metadata.description:
Frozen benchmark, partitioning protocols, baselines, stored predictions and analysis code accompanying the manuscript TCR-IMAP: Homology-Controlled Evaluation of TCR–MHC Contact Prediction.

The contribution is the evaluation framework. The archive contains the apparatus for measuring how much of a sequence-based TCR–MHC class I contact predictor's apparent accuracy belongs to the evaluation rather than to the model: 174 curated TCR–peptide–MHC class I complexes, all with a human MHC class I heavy chain, collapsing to 69 TCR clusters at a similarity ratio of 0.70; contact labels and candidate masks over a 174 × 75 × 84 tensor holding 893,928 resolved residue pairs of which 5,281 (0.59 %) are contacts at a 4.5 Å heavy-atom threshold, keyed by IMGT number together with insertion code; five partitioning protocols fixed before the reported results were produced, with a declared primary metric, protocol and comparison; within-fold pair-frequency priors; complete stored pairwise predictions for all five protocols; per-complex per-residue metrics; comparator reimplementations with a full provenance and deviation table; a training-size-matched control whose plan was committed before any downsampled model was trained; the authoritative identity-threshold sweep at 20,000 cluster-bootstrap resamples; and the molecular-dynamics analysis code with its twelve output tables.

A worked example reproduces the reported pairwise results from the stored arrays on a CPU in under a minute. Retraining is optional and needs a GPU.

Scope and limitations. Paired αβ TCRs on human MHC class I, α1/α2 platform; receptors are human in 165 complexes, mouse in 8 and mixed chimpanzee/human α in 1. MHC class II, γδ receptors and non-human MHC are out of scope. The archive contains no sequence-to-input builder: applying the model outside the cohort requires an IMGT numbering step that is documented but not implemented. The predeclared primary comparison is unresolved at this sample size (+0.0312 [−0.0049, +0.0650], p = 0.088) and is reported as it stands. The canonical-CDR-only sensitivity covers 14 comparisons but not that primary comparison, because the per-residue benchmark stores metrics rather than predictions and writes no checkpoint; no historical per-residue checkpoint or prediction array exists. Molecular-dynamics trajectories are not included. Source structures are from STCRDab and the Protein Data Bank and are referenced, not redistributed.
